items.stem: A question requires chaining three related facts across documents. Flat vector RAG returns disconnected chunks. Why does GraphRAG help?

options.text: Graph traversal follows relationships between entities to assemble multi-hop context
options.rationale: Correct: traversal connects related facts that flat retrieval leaves disconnected.

options.text: Graphs guarantee the answer is correct
options.rationale: They improve context, not guarantee correctness.

items.explanation: Correct: traversal connects related facts that flat retrieval leaves disconnected.

items.stem: Which TWO steps improve a knowledge graph built from raw text? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Resolve duplicate entities that refer to the same thing
options.rationale: Correct: entity resolution prevents fragmented, wrong traversals.

options.text: Design the schema to fit the questions you must answer
options.rationale: Correct: schema fit to queries makes traversal useful.

options.text: Accept every extracted relation as true
Rebuild the entire graph on every tiny change
options.rationale: Full rebuilds are wasteful; prefer incremental updates.

items.explanation: Correct: entity resolution prevents fragmented, wrong traversals.

items.stem: A GraphRAG answer states a relationship that does not exist in the graph. What is the correct safeguard?

options.text: Ground answers strictly in traversed facts and flag unsupported claims
options.rationale: Correct: answers must be grounded in the graph, not invented.

options.text: Allow the model to add plausible relationships
Remove grounding to speed up answers
Trust the answer because the graph exists
options.rationale: Existence of a graph does not prevent hallucination.

items.explanation: Correct: answers must be grounded in the graph, not invented.
